reason: This is the last compile error. Field default values (`= ...`) only work on nightly Rust, and `"Hello World"` is a `&str`, not a `String`. `SimpleLoginScreen::new()` already sets the title to "Hello World".
The app is built but never started, so no window opens. Calling `run()` opens the 800x600 window and prints the login screen.
`withLoginButtonOfColor` has nowhere to keep the colour, so for now it only prints it. Adding a field lets the screen remember it (it's a `String` for now; a colour type can come later).
`Mode` is no longer used now that you write `Windowed` directly (via `use window::Mode::*;`), so this line causes an unused-import warning.
`run()` blocks until the window closes and returns nothing, so `app` is never used and causes a warning. Calling the chain directly does the same thing.

An empty `enum Color {}` has no values, so nothing can be stored in `login_button_color`. To get it compiling without changing your line, I wrapped it in a `named_colors!` macro that adds the variants behind the scenes. If you write the variants out yourself, the code says what it means, and I can then remove the macro wrapper.
with: pub enum Color { Grey, Red, Green, Blue }
